‼️ The CLARITY Act won’t move markets 

🔖 Forget short-term price charts – Washington’s digital asset framework is the legal authorization that conservative wealth managers have been waiting for before they can put trillions to work. Everyone seems to be watching the CLARITY Act for the same thing. From retail traders to institutional giants, people are waiting for the green light that confirms Washington has clarified the market. Legislation doesn’t move markets through a single, uniform mechanism. 

☄️ The GENIUS Act has limitations on a single-asset framework for payment stablecoins. CLARITY works at a different layer: a horizontal market-structure bill covering how digital assets are classified, who regulates them, and who is allowed to custody and trade them.

⁉️ That’s why its success shouldn’t be benchmarked against a single price chart. The metric that matters here is the slower signal underneath: custody mandates being written, treasury policies being rewritten, allocation committees granting their first approvals.

⚠️ That’s the real story. The CLARITY Act is fundamentally a legal permission structure. By handing institutional wealth managers and world-class operators the regulatory green light they need to enter the room, this law achieves something more durable than a market rally. It moves the people who build markets, not just the capital.

📝A Zoo of Robots📝
Chinese drones are becoming more sophisticated

The sphere of unmanned technologies in China continues to advance by leaps and bounds. Not a month passes without new footage appearing featuring well-known robodogs — they are frequently used during military exercises in the country. And, it appears, the Chinese military will soon have an entire "zoo" in its arsenal.

Last year, the PLA's National Defense Science and Technology University demonstrated a robot created in the image of an insect. The device consists of a narrow fuselage, two "wings," and three supports — its length is estimated at approximately two centimeters. There are no signs of mass production yet; the "mosquito" remains a laboratory prototype.

The developers call such systems suitable for reconnaissance and special operations. They also mentioned another four-winged prototype that can be controlled from a smartphone. However, China has not disclosed the exact specifications of the communication system, range, flight time, and installed equipment.

📌The idea itself is not new. For example, the Norwegian-American Black Hornet has long been used as a reconnaissance drone by both NATO military personnel and the AFU. The Chinese are following the same path, while simultaneously attempting to make the device even smaller and less detectable by detection systems.

🖍But miniaturization remains the main limitation for now. Into a body the size of an insect, one must fit a power source, a control system, and a payload, and every extra milligram reduces flight time and worsens stability.

❗️Such a device will be particularly vulnerable outdoors. Wind, rain, and dust pose serious problems for a machine weighing fractions of a gram. Therefore, the appearance of the "mosquito" should be viewed as a demonstration of China's technological ambitions, as they closely observe the latest trends in modern conflicts.

Rabí Castle, Czech Republic

Founded around 1350, Rabí Castle rises above the Otava River and evolved into a magnificent residence for the Lords of Rýzmberk throughout the 14th and 15th centuries.

It remained a lived-in home until the late 1600s. Then, in the early 1700s, a devastating fire destroyed its roofs and wooden interiors. Over time, locals repurposed its stones and materials, leaving the structure in ruins.

Since the 1950s, the Czech state has held ownership, and in 1978, it was officially designated a National Cultural Heritage site. From 2013 onward, management has been entrusted to the National Heritage Institute.

Today, Rabí Castle welcomes visitors with guided tours and hosts cultural events, including concerts, theater performances, and puppet shows.
